title: Component Labs: Guided migration recipes and live examples for tokens, controls, tables, charts
creator: Asha Nair
description: Create a set of interactive 'Component Labs' pages and guided migration recipes that demonstrate best practices for migrating to our updated design tokens and modernized component APIs. Focus components: tokens, Button variants, responsive Tables, and accessible Charts. Deliverables include live-editable examples, before/after migration toggles, short do/don't reference cards per component, codemod instructions, sample pull requests, and a brief QA checklist for platform engineers. The goal is to reduce migration friction for product teams and lower support tickets caused by token name/scale changes and API surface differences.
tasks: Design interactive lab templates (token playground, control knobs, table data toggles, chart dataset switcher)
Author migration recipes: token mapping matrix, spacing/scale reconciliation, color role substitutions
Implement before/after toggles that swap legacy CSS variables with new token names in runtime
Add live code editor snippets for React + Vanilla usage (init, props, common gotchas)
Write codemod examples (jscodeshift + sed examples) and include safety notes
Coordinate with engineering to create two sample migration PRs and link them
Create accessibility guidance for tables and charts (keyboard focus, aria, high-contrast mode)
Ship documentation pages to docsite and verify in staging environment
Collect and resolve initial reviewer feedback from PM and Runtime engineers
acceptance_criteria: Four Component Lab pages (Tokens, Buttons, Tables, Charts) are merged to docsite-2026.03 and accessible from Design System landing page
Each page contains at least three live-editable examples showing legacy vs new token/API, with copyable code snippets
A token mapping CSV and a one-shot codemod example are attached and validated on two sample repos
DO / DON'T cards exist for each component and are reviewed by Accessibility champion
Two sample PR links demonstrate common migration scenarios and include CI passing in staging
Design and Engineering sign-off recorded in comments with a final checklist entry

notes: Trade-offs discussed: full auto-migration is tempting, but fragile across private installs. Provide opt-in codemods and robust verification steps instead.
Decision: Use a lightweight React playground (codesandbox-like iframe) for live edits to minimize docsite bundle size. Static fallback screenshots included for customers that block scripts.
Performance note: toggling tokens in runtime should avoid layout thrash. We implemented CSS custom properties and batch DOM updates in a single requestAnimationFrame.
Future: consider a 'Migration Assistant' CLI that runs token diffs across repo and reports likely impacted files (out of scope for this ticket).
